headline: US stocks closed higher, breaking four-day slide as cooling oil prices offset hotter August CPI and reinforced expectations of a Fed rate hike next week
raw_text:
- The S&P 500 ($SPX) rose 0.86% to 7,656.98, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) gained 0.98% to 52,573.29, and the Nasdaq ($COMP) advanced 0.96% to 26,333.04, snapping a four-day losing streak
- August CPI increased 0.4% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, while core CPI rose 0.3% and came in hotter than forecasts, according to the BLS and Reuters (TRI)
- CME FedWatch data showed around 90% odds that the Federal Reserve will raise rates at its September 17 meeting following the hotter CPI print
- Brent crude (@QA) fell nearly 3% from recent highs above $108 to roughly $104–105 per barrel, easing some inflation concerns tied to Middle East tensions
- Technology hardware led gains after Oracle reported a fiscal Q1 beat and raised guidance, with cloud revenue up 62% to $11.6 billion and AI infrastructure up 121%
- Dell (DELL) climbed about 12% to a record high, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) jumped 12%, HP (HPQ) rose 8.4%, and Oracle declined 1.7% as investors digested Oracle’s (ORCL) cloud and AI strength
- Sector-wise, technology (XLK) gained roughly 1.3%, communication services was supported by Charter Communications (CHTR) and T-Mobile (TMUS), while utilities lagged as XLU (XLU) slipped about 0.3% on higher yields pressuring PG&E (PCG) and American Water Works (AWK)
- ACV Auctions (ACVA) surged around 44% after Copart (CPRT) agreed to acquire the company for $10.50 per share, representing a roughly 45% premium
- Zumiez (ZUMZ) fell 16% after reporting a wider-than-expected Q2 loss and weak sales, while NuScale Power (SMR) dropped about 15.7% with no specific catalyst cited
- Adobe (ADBE) edged lower despite a Q3 earnings beat as investors weighed AI monetization risks, and traders now focus on next week’s Fed rate decision, retail sales data, and additional earnings releases
